entries.title: Haka style Jerk Chicken
entries.answer: Haka style Jerk Chicken is one of our mains ($22). Herb and spice steeped chicken leg quarter. Cooled, battered then fried with rice and peas, steamed cabbage and sweet plantain. Served with Tamarind sauce.

entries.title: Mojo Criollo Shrimp
entries.answer: Mojo Criollo Shrimp is one of our mains ($26). Jumbo Shrimp sautéed in a savory citrus orange, lime and garlic sauce served with a Corn and Carrot Yellow Rice Risotto.

entries.title: Shrimp Milanesa
entries.answer: Shrimp Milanesa is one of our mains ($30). Chopped and Formed Shrimp Cutlet, Fried Crisp. Topped with a fresh arugula salad.

entries.title: Porchetta Pernil
entries.answer: Porchetta Pernil is one of our mains ($34). Porchetta seasoned Dominican Pernil style served with garlic green beans, Yucca Mofongo (mashed cassava) and sweet plantain.

entries.title: What is jerk?
entries.answer: Jerk is Jamaica’s famous way of seasoning and cooking: meat is marinated in a paste of allspice (pimento), Scotch bonnet pepper, scallion, thyme and garlic, then traditionally cooked low and smoky over pimento wood. On our menu you’ll find the Haka style Jerk Chicken, the Jerk Chicken Arugula Flat Bread and Jerk Apricot wings. Heat varies by dish; several items are marked on the menu, like the Chicken Pumpkin soup (no spice) and the Shrimp Butternut Bisque (light spice). Not sure? Give us a call at 508-801-5444.

entries.title: Scotch bonnet
entries.answer: The Scotch bonnet is the signature Caribbean pepper: very hot (in the same range as a habanero) with a fruity, almost sweet flavor. We use it in our Scotch Bonnet Honey, which tops the Jerk Chicken Arugula Flat Bread and is one of our Crispy Wings flavors (Sweet & Spicy).

entries.title: Plantains & tostones
entries.answer: Plantains are a Caribbean staple. Ripe ones are fried sweet and caramelized (maduros); green ones are smashed and twice-fried into crunchy tostones. Sweet plantain comes with our Haka style Jerk Chicken and our Porchetta Pernil. Tostones aren’t on our current menu.

entries.title: Mofongo
entries.answer: Mofongo is a beloved Caribbean mash, classically fried green plantain pounded with garlic and pork cracklings. Ours is a Yucca Mofongo (mashed cassava) served with the Porchetta Pernil.

entries.title: Mangú
entries.answer: Mangú is the Dominican Republic’s comfort food: boiled green plantains mashed smooth with butter and topped with pickled red onions, often served as “los tres golpes” with fried salami, fried cheese and eggs. It isn’t on our current menu.

entries.title: Sofrito & sazón
entries.answer: Sofrito is the aromatic base of so much Caribbean cooking, a blend of peppers, onion, garlic and herbs. Sazón is a seasoning mix, often with annatto (achiote), cumin, coriander, garlic and oregano, and adobo is an all-purpose garlic-and-spice seasoning. You’ll taste that family of flavors in dishes like our Caribbean Caesar with adobo limón dressing.

entries.title: Rice and peas
entries.answer: Jamaican rice and peas is rice simmered with red kidney beans (the “peas”), coconut milk, thyme, scallion and allspice. It comes with our Haka style Jerk Chicken, along with steamed cabbage and sweet plantain. The Mojo Criollo Shrimp comes with a Corn and Carrot Yellow Rice Risotto.

entries.title: Mojo criollo
entries.answer: Mojo criollo is a bright Caribbean marinade of citrus, garlic and herbs. Our Mojo Criollo Shrimp is jumbo shrimp sautéed in a savory citrus orange, lime and garlic sauce, served with a Corn and Carrot Yellow Rice Risotto. Mojo Criollo is also one of our Crispy Wings flavors.

entries.title: Pernil
entries.answer: Pernil is slow-roasted, garlicky pork shoulder, a centerpiece of Dominican and Puerto Rican celebrations. Our Porchetta Pernil is porchetta seasoned Dominican Pernil style, served with garlic green beans, Yucca Mofongo and sweet plantain.

entries.title: Ackee and saltfish
entries.answer: Ackee and saltfish is Jamaica’s national dish: the buttery ackee fruit sautéed with salted cod, onion, tomato and peppers. It isn’t on our current menu, but it’s a classic worth knowing.

entries.title: Oxtail
entries.answer: Jamaican oxtail is slow-braised until fall-off-the-bone tender with allspice, thyme, browning and butter beans. It isn’t on our current menu.

entries.title: Curry goat
entries.answer: Curry goat is a Jamaican celebration dish: goat stewed with Caribbean curry powder, thyme, scallion and Scotch bonnet, usually with rice. It isn’t on our current menu.

entries.title: Festival
entries.answer: Festival is a slightly sweet Jamaican fried dumpling made with cornmeal and flour, a classic partner for fried fish or jerk. It isn’t on our current menu.

entries.title: Sancocho
entries.answer: Sancocho is the Dominican Republic’s hearty celebration stew of several meats with yuca, plantain, corn and other root vegetables. It isn’t on our current menu, but we do have two soups: Chicken Pumpkin (no spice) and Shrimp Butternut Bisque (light spice).

entries.title: Chimichurri burger
entries.answer: A Dominican “chimi” (chimichurri burger) is a street-food favorite: a seasoned patty on soft bread with shredded cabbage, onion, tomato and a creamy sauce. It isn’t on our current menu.

entries.title: Morir soñando
entries.answer: Morir soñando (“to die dreaming”) is a classic Dominican refresher of orange juice and milk with sugar and lots of ice. It isn’t on our posted menu.

entries.title: Tamarind
entries.answer: Tamarind is a tangy-sweet tropical pod used across the Caribbean. Our Haka style Jerk Chicken is served with Tamarind sauce, and Sweet (Tamarind) is one of our Crispy Wings flavors.

entries.title: Where we are
entries.answer: We’re at 71 Water St, Woods Hole, MA 02543, right on Eel Pond, a short walk from the Steamship Authority ferry terminal. Parking in the village is limited (metered street spots fill up fast in summer), so walking, biking the Shining Sea Bikeway or allowing extra time is a good idea.

entries.title: Dietary & allergies
entries.answer: On our menu, the Cheese Personal Pizza and the Vermont Brussels have no meat listed, and the Caribbean Caesar can be ordered without the chicken or shrimp add-ons. For gluten-free needs and any allergies, please call us at 508-801-5444 before you visit so we can talk through ingredients with you.

entries.title: Our menu
entries.answer: We serve island-inspired Caribbean and Latin plates. Starters: Soup, Flat Bread (7”), Personal Pizza (7”), Popcorn Shrimp, Vermont Brussels, Crispy Wings, Empanadas, Caribbean Caesar. Mains: Haka style Jerk Chicken, Mojo Criollo Shrimp, Shrimp Milanesa, Porchetta Pernil. Starters run about $10 to $16 and mains $22 to $34. Scroll up to the Menu section for every detail.

entries.title: Caribbean flavors
entries.answer: Our kitchen draws on Caribbean and Latin flavors: Jamaican jerk and Scotch bonnet heat, Dominican pernil, mofongo and sweet plantain, citrusy mojo criollo, tamarind and adobo. Ask me about any of them!
